questions.prompt: Why is nationality insufficient to predict communication preference?
questions.answer: People participate in multiple contexts and individuals vary.
Recognising limits, seeking appropriate guidance and adapting respectfully.
questions.feedback: Do not demand personal identity disclosure.

questions.prompt: Can a customary practice be questioned?
questions.answer: Yes, especially when access, safety or legitimate obligations are affected.

questions.prompt: What is a better explanation than 'they are just like that'?
questions.answer: A bounded description of observed practice and possible contextual conditions.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only; use answer-specific feedback.
scoring.practice: Compares contextual explanations and adapts communication respectfully without demographic stereotyping.
scoring.transfer: Design an inclusive communication plan for a fictional group bringing together different roles and communication preferences. Include an actual procedure, a way to verify unfamiliar practices, an access alternative and a boundary that preserves dignity and safety.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
